standard_prerequisites.name: Enumerable and nonenumerable
standard_prerequisites.statement: A set is enumerable when it is empty or there is a surjective function from the positive integers onto it; a set is nonenumerable when it is not enumerable.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted theorem asserts nonenumerability, and the proof establishes it by showing every list of subsets omits a subset.

standard_prerequisites.name: Power set
standard_prerequisites.statement: The power set of a set X is the set of all subsets of X.
standard_prerequisites.use: The listed objects N_0, N_1, ... are subsets of the natural numbers, and the constructed D must be one of them (1266-1268).

standard_prerequisites.name: Equality of sets
standard_prerequisites.statement: Two sets are equal when they have the same elements; they differ when some element belongs to one and not to the other.
standard_prerequisites.use: D is separated from each N_n by the element n, whose membership in D is the opposite of its membership in N_n (1270-1273).

core_obligations: Suppose a list N_0, N_1, N_2, ... of subsets of the natural numbers is given (1264-1265).
Define D as the set of those natural numbers n with n not in N_n (1266-1268).
Observe D is a subset of the natural numbers, hence a member of the power set (1269).

For each n, membership of n in D is by construction the negation of membership of n in N_n, so D differs from N_n as a set; hence D is not on the list, and no enumeration of the power set exists (1270-1273).

proof_roadmap.step: Take an arbitrary list of subsets of the natural numbers.
Define the diagonal set D by flipping membership at the matching index.
Show D is a subset missing from the list and conclude nonenumerability.

difficulty_reason: The counted theorem is the author theorem at source lines 1213-1216: the power set of the natural numbers is not enumerable. The author proof (1218-1229) carries the diagonal idea without an array: given an arbitrary list of subsets of the natural numbers it defines the set D of those n that are absent from the n-th listed subset, observes D is a subset of the natural numbers, and shows D differs from every listed subset at the point n. The definition of D and the membership flip that separates D from each N_n are the load-bearing steps, so the unit is a real construction rather than a definition unpacking.
